correctness.rationale: For each line the intersection weight sum is 12. A line with no quintuple point must have six triple points and no double. Exhaustive two-quintuple cases (whether AB is a line) give 15,16,18 triples; pair counting determines n2. Under (15,11,0,3), all 13 lines have six singular points; at least two quintuple connectors occur, and the two-connector and three-connector cases yield contradictions. A root-of-unity construction and exact GF(11) checker verify the middle profile, though the universal proof is symbolic.

value.rationale: The exact 13-line, maximal multiplicity five case is the initiating paper's unresolved boundary. Two of fifteen explicitly retained candidate weak profiles are shown unrealizable by structural pencil incidence arguments, eliminating the sole three-quintuple case and obtaining a sharp two-quintuple trichotomy with a realized Fermat case. This isolates meaningful realizability restrictions beyond numerical Tjurina arithmetic.
